meta.title: Mumbai property-tax payment (current year, residential, known property account number) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the instant-payment route is public but was read only, with no property account number entered and no payment attempted; the citizen login is gated by a property account number and a CAPTCHA, and was not crossed; the newest rate schedule published on the corporation's own capital-value route takes effect from 1 April 2015 and the companion capital-value fixation rules run only to 2019-20, so no reviewed route confirms the rate for the current financial year; the portal's own FAQ page renders a heading and no content. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

scenarios.label: Mumbai property-tax payment on a known property account number
scenarios.summary: An individual owner pays the current year's property tax on a residential property already on the municipal register with a known identifier, by the municipal payment route, online portal first and counter or bank route second. First-time assessment, name transfer or mutation, arrears disputes, rebate eligibility beyond what the payment route itself states, and commercial property are excluded.

sources.title: Citizen Portal Services, Property Tax - login and information page
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'Citizen Portal Services - Property Tax' under the MCGM logo, with the banner 'BMC'S CAPITAL VALUE BASED PROPERTY TAX INFORMATION SYSTEM'. Direct current observation of a public official interface, reached without login; it shows no visible last-updated or version date. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20260309232045/https://ptaxportal.mcgm.gov.in/CitizenPortal/ (2026-03-09); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Rates of Taxation on Capital Value with effect from 01.04.2015 - Assessment & Collection Department
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'BRIHANMUMBAI MAHANAGARPALIKA (Assessment & Collection Department)'. Four pages; the effective date printed on every page is 01.04.2015 and is recorded as publishedAt. Graded C as potentially outdated official material: nothing later is published on the same route, and the companion capital-value fixation rules there cover only 2015-16 to 2019-20. Archive: the Wayback availability API returned no snapshot for this file on the access date, so no archive copy exists to point to; the original official URL is retained and the capture failure is recorded here as a limitation. No new capture was pushed from this run.

claims.text: The Assessment & Collection Department's published rates of taxation on capital value, with effect from 1 April 2015, give the residential user category a general tax including fire tax of 0.110 per cent, water tax 0.253 per cent, water benefit tax 0.069 per cent, sewerage tax 0.163 per cent, sewerage benefit tax 0.043 per cent, municipal education cess 0.040 per cent, state education cess 0.035 per cent, employment guarantee cess 0.010 per cent, tree cess 0.002 per cent and street tax 0.050 per cent.
claims.notes: An actionable fee schedule: percentages a citizen applies to the capital value of a residential property. Graded C because currency is not established by any reviewed route.

claims.text: The corporation's capital-value document index publishes rate and rule files whose latest coverage is the rates effective from 1 April 2015 and the rules for fixation of capital value for 2015-16 to 2019-20, with no document covering any later financial year.
claims.notes: Checkable from the index's own file list on the access date. The current financial year is 2026-27.

claims.text: The property-tax portal states that the citizen enters the Property Account No. to log in, that the number is shown on the upper portion of the property tax bill, and that a Search button is provided to find it.
claims.notes: A usable rule for the identifier this scenario assumes the owner already has.

claims.text: The published rate schedule sets out separate tables by user category, with residential user in Table No. 1 and commercial, industrial and other users in Table No. 2.
claims.notes: A rule that decides which rate applies to this scenario's residential property.

claims.text: The property-tax portal publishes an Instant Payment route reachable without login, which displays the property account number, billing name, property address, an outstanding-bill breakdown into property tax, GPR, repair cess and MTOB, and the outstanding, discount, net and advance amounts, alongside an online payment action.
claims.notes: The route's own field labels were observed. No property account number was entered, so nothing is claimed about what it returns for a real property.

claims.text: The Instant Payment route states that online payment is applied on a first-in first-out basis, with the oldest bill adjusted first, and that a citizen wishing to pay against a specific bill should contact the Assessment & Collection department of the respective ward.
claims.notes: A rule about how a payment is applied, and a named office to approach when it is not what the citizen wants.

claims.text: The property-tax portal's public entry page publishes a table headed 'E-mail IDs of Asstt. Assessor & Collector of wards' giving one e-mail address for each of the corporation's wards.
claims.notes: A specific office list with a contact route for the role that assesses and collects, indexed by ward. Institutional addresses only; no personal data recorded.

claims.text: The property-tax portal states that registration of KYC does not change the billing name or owner name and only allows the property owner to access the property account number on the portal after authorisation through an OTP.
claims.notes: Recorded for the boundary it draws between this scenario and the excluded name-change route.

claims.text: The property-tax portal offers a tax calculator described on its own entry page as being for any hypothetical example.
claims.notes: The calculator was not exercised; only the corporation's own description of it is recorded.

claims.text: The property-tax portal's Contact Us route gives only the corporation's headquarters address at Mumbai C.S.T. 400001 and a portal feedback e-mail address, with no property-tax office, officer or telephone number.
The property-tax portal's FAQ route rendered the heading 'FAQ' and no questions, answers or other content on the access date.
claims.notes: Direct current observation, recorded as observed rather than treated as a page that merely failed to load: the heading rendered and the body did not.

claims.text: The property-tax portal's citizen login requires a property account number and a CAPTCHA, so the account view of bills and receipts is not visible on any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Boundary statement, recorded as a limitation and not used to support any positive cell value. The observation is the login form; the inference is that the account view lies past it. No CAPTCHA was attempted.

claims.text: What the citizen is shown or given after paying property tax, whether a receipt, an acknowledgement or a status route, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related in origin: the instant-payment route is public and was simply not carried through, because completing a payment is outside the safety boundary.

claims.text: When the current year's property tax falls due, and whether any rebate or penalty attaches to paying early or late, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.
